verdict.rationale: Adyen documents custom risk rules built around your business's fraud risks, risk lists that act on your own data (uploadable through the Referrals API), and a fraud data collection SDK you can add to your site. So merchant-specific data does shape risk decisions. However, the machine-learning scoring is described as running on Adyen's global transaction data, and nothing shows you can feed it your own signals. Missing for 10: evidence that merchant-supplied device fingerprints, behavioral data or custom metadata feed the ML score; documentation of which signals the data collection SDK captures; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can feed the model my own signals — device fingerprints, behavioral data, custom metadata — so scoring reflects my business, not just network defaults

citations.quote: Build your own custom risk rules around the unique fraud risks faced by your business.
let you block or allow a transaction based on Adyen's data, your own data, or lists provided by third parties.
